title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It captures principles, concrete rules, SLOs, enforcement, and a short set of ADRs that record recent decisions. The goal is a single canonical reference for engineers and architects planning or reviewing services and model integrations.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all service and runtime teams that operate customer-facing APIs, the serving runtime, Dedicated and Private deployments, and platform integrations (Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Console, and Optimize). Excludes: experimental research prototypes not intended for production.

Principles
----------
- API compatibility: Backwards-compatible changes by default; breaking changes require an ADR and a 60-day deprecation window.
- Observability first: All production services must emit traces, metrics, and structured logs for top-level requests.
- Performance-aware: Design for predictable p99 latency and cost per token (where applicable).
- Secure-by-default: Least privilege, encrypted-in-transit and at-rest for customer data, and RBAC controls for management planes.
- Reuse & composability: Prefer shared libraries and internal frameworks for common concerns (auth, telemetry, retry/fallback).

API Standards
-------------
Overview:
- All public and internal REST APIs must follow the OpenAPI 3.1 specification. Where the API is RPC/chat/streaming-first, provide an OpenAPI facade and API contract.
- Versioning: Use path-based major versioning (/v1/...). Minor changes must be additive.
- Authentication: Bearer tokens (OAuth2 or API keys) + service-to-service mTLS for internal control-plane calls.
- Rate limiting: Use per-token and per-account quotas enforced at API gateway (default: 100 reqs/s per account, configurable for Enterprise).

Standard Response Shape (JSON):
- success: {"ok": true, "data": ... }
- error: {"ok": false, "error": {"code": "ERR_xxx", "message": "human-friendly", "details": {}}}

Best practices:
1. Provide clear error codes and machine-readable details for programmatic clients.
2. Implement idempotency keys for mutation endpoints.
3. Support streaming for long-running generation responses with chunked transfer and event framing (Server-Sent Events or HTTP/2 chunking).
4. Document rate limits and retry guidance in the API spec.

Coding Standards
----------------
- Language support: primary services should be implemented in Go or Python depending on latency and developer ergonomics (Go for latencies <50ms p50, Python for glue and orchestration).
- Formatting & linting: lint + format enforced by CI (gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/ruff/flake8 for Python).
- Static analysis: enable critical linters and SCA tools in CI; block merges on high severity findings.
- Tests: unit (>80% coverage target for core modules), integration tests for service contracts, and end-to-end smoke tests in pre-prod.
- Dependency policy: no direct pull of pre-release model-serving runtimes into production images; use curated images from the internal image registry.

Infra Standards
---------------
- IaC: Terraform for cloud infra; modules must follow naming & tagging scheme: team:<team-name>, service:<service-name>, env:<env>.
- Networking: All production control-plane traffic must be isolated in VPCs and use NAT gateways for outbound egress where required by compliance.
- Secrets: Use KMS/HSM-backed secrets (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM for on-prem). No plaintext secrets in repos.
- Capacity & autoscaling: GPU pools for model serving must expose target utilization metrics; autoscaling policies must include cooldowns and safety caps.

Model-Serving Standards
----------------------
- Model packaging: All model artifacts must include manifest.json with model id, version, architecture, tokenizer, quantization profile, and expected memory & FLOP footprint.
- Execution profile: Record and publish perf profile (latency by sequence length, memory, token throughput) as part of model onboarding.
- Quantization: Maintain and document supported quantization profiles (fp16, int8, int4) and recommended use-cases.
- Fallbacks: Define compatible fallback model variants for each production model (e.g., full-precision fallback for quality-critical endpoints).
- Rolling upgrades: Canary 5% traffic for 24 hours, 25% for 12 hours, then 100% if metrics are green. Automatic rollback on p50/p95/p99 regressions or error-rate spikes (see Performance SLOs).

Observability Standards
----------------------
- Tracing: All external-facing requests must propagate W3C Trace Context; traces should include model id/version, route, and route-specific attributes (e.g., prompt-length, token-count, batching-id).
- Metrics (Prometheus):
  - service_request_duration_seconds (histogram) with labels {route, model, outcome}
  - service_request_errors_total (counter) with labels {route, model, error_code}
  - model_inference_latency_seconds (histogram) with labels {model, sequence_length}
  - gpu_utilization_percent (gauge) with labels {host, pool}
- Logging: Structured JSON logs at severity levels. Sensitive fields must be redacted before writing (prompt text redaction for customer-provided PII unless explicitly allowed).
- Dashboards & alerts: Per-route dashboards for latency, error rates, and cost-per-token. Alerts: page on p99 latency > SLO by 2x sustained 5m or error rate > 1% for 10m.

Performance Standards & SLOs
---------------------------
- Default SLOs for public API routes (can be overridden per product):
  - Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime (excluding scheduled maintenance)
  - Latency: p50 < 100ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms for request/response (non-streaming short prompts).
  - Quality: no automated regressions in model outputs for monitored eval prompt sets (daily regression checks).
- Cost targets: Provide cost-per-token targets per model family in the model catalog and track against Optimize recommendations.

Performance measurement table (example):

| Metric                         | Target                        | Alert Threshold                  |
|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Availability (monthly)         | >= 99.9%                      | < 99.7%                         |
| p95 latency (short prompts)    | < 350ms                       | > 700ms sustained 5m            |
| Model inference p99 (long)     | < 1.5s                        | > 3.0s                          |
| Error rate (5m window)         | < 0.5%                        | > 1.0%                          |

Decision Records (ADRs)
------------------------
- ADR-2025-09: Standardized API versioning scheme (path-based major versions). Owner: API Platform. Status: accepted.
- ADR-2025-11: Choose Go as primary low-latency service language for core inference control plane. Owner: Eng Infrastructure. Status: accepted.
- ADR-2026-01: Use W3C Trace Context for distributed tracing and include model metadata in trace attributes. Owner: Observability. Status: accepted.

Example ADR format (template):
1. Title: ADR-YYYY-NN Short Title
2. Context: Why this decision matters, alternatives considered.
3. Decision: The chosen option.
4. Consequences: Short- and long-term impacts, migration steps.

Governance, Rollout & Enforcement
--------------------------------
- Ownership: Each standard area has an owning team (API Platform, Eng Platform, Eng Infra, Observability, Applied ML). Owners are responsible for reviews and updates.
- Review cadence: Quarterly reviews for standards; urgent security/perf changes may be pushed at any time with cross-team notification.
- CI gates: Linting, spec validation (OpenAPI), and telemetry instrumentation checks are required for merges to main for production services.
- Exceptions: Temporary exceptions must be recorded in the architecture exceptions registry and approved by the owning team; exceptions expire after 90 days unless renewed.

Operational Runbook (high-level)
-------------------------------
1. On service deployment: verify OpenAPI contract, confirm telemetry ingestion (traces, metrics), ensure automated health checks pass.
2. On performance regression (alert): run canary rollback to previous model/service variant, open incident and notify SRE + Product + Model owners.
3. Postmortem: within 72 hours of major incident, produce postmortem with owner, timeline, impact, root cause, and action items.

Appendix: Quick reference snippets
--------------------------------
OpenAPI validation (CI):
  curl -sS https://ci.internal/validate-openapi -F file=@openapi.yaml || exit 1

Example model manifest.json (required keys):
  {
    "model_id": "gptx-13b",
    "version": "2026-01-12",
    "architecture": "transformer",
    "tokenizer": "bpe-v2",
    "quant_profiles": ["fp16", "int8"],
    "memory_bytes_estimate": 43000000000,
    "perf_profile_url": "s3://model-catalog/perf/gptx-13b/2026-01-12.json"
  }
